newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat Auto denies Rivalta plant to close.
newsitem.headline: Fiat Auto denies Rivalta plant to close.

text.p: Italian carmaker Fiat Auto on Wednesday denied strongly a newspaper report that its Rivalta car plant in Turin was about to be closed.

In a statement, Fiat Auto said that it "denied most categorically" a report in the Rome-base La Repubblica newspaper that Rivalta was to close. It added that by the end of 1997, Rivalta would see the return of temporary workers transferred to Fiat's other Turin plant at Mirafiori which would boost Rivalta's workforce to 6,200, up 1,100 from current levels.
Car production at Fiat's Rivalta plant includes the Lancia Delta, Dedra and K, and from the end of June it will move to two shifts, ahead of the scheduled move planned for December.
By the end of the year, the Rivalta plant will also start production work for the top of the range Alfa Romeo, the new Alfa 164, due for commercial launch in the spring of 1998.
